fluency-training.name: Reading Fluency Training
fluency-training.description: Practice reading passages with speed, accuracy, and proper expression

levels.name: Short Passages
levels.instructions: Read the passage aloud at your natural pace. Time yourself and track your words per minute.

exercises.passage: The sun rises in the east each morning. It brings light to the world. Birds sing in the trees. The day begins with new hope.
Water flows down the river. Fish swim in the clear water. Trees grow along the bank. The river moves to the sea.

levels.name: Medium Passages
levels.instructions: Read the passage aloud with proper expression. Time yourself and track your words per minute.

exercises.passage: The ancient forest was home to many creatures. Tall trees reached for the sky, their leaves creating a green canopy. Birds nested in the branches, singing their morning songs. Deer walked quietly through the underbrush, alert for any danger.

Science teaches us about the world. Through observation and experiment, we discover how things work. From the smallest atoms to the largest galaxies, everything follows natural laws. Curiosity drives scientists to ask questions and seek answers.

levels.name: Long Passages
levels.instructions: Read the passage aloud with good pacing and expression. Time yourself and track your words per minute.

exercises.passage: The city library stood at the heart of the town, its stone walls weathered by time. Inside, shelves lined every wall, filled with books of every kind. People of all ages came to read, study, and learn. The librarian knew every book and could help anyone find what they needed. It was a place of quiet discovery and endless knowledge.

Understanding how the brain learns to read is fascinating. When we read, multiple brain regions work together. Visual areas recognize letters, language areas process sounds and meanings, and memory areas connect new information with what we already know. With practice, reading becomes automatic and effortless.

comprehension-strategies.name: Reading Comprehension Strategies
comprehension-strategies.description: Practice strategies to understand and remember what you read

levels.name: Main Idea Identification
levels.instructions: Read the passage and identify the main idea from the options

exercises.passage: Dogs are loyal companions. They provide comfort and protection to their owners. Many people consider dogs part of their family.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
exercises.hint: Look for the most important point

exercises.passage: The sun provides light and warmth to Earth. Plants need sunlight to grow. Animals depend on plants for food.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: The sun is important for life
exercises.hint: Think about what connects all the sentences

exercises.passage: Reading every day improves vocabulary. It also helps with spelling. Regular reading makes you a better writer.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of this passage?

levels.name: Making Inferences
levels.instructions: Read the passage and make logical inferences

exercises.passage: Sarah looked out the window and frowned. She grabbed her umbrella and put on her raincoat.
exercises.question: What can you infer about the weather?
options: It is raining or about to rain

exercises.passage: The boy studied every night for a week. When he got his test back, he smiled broadly.
exercises.question: What can you infer about the test?
options: He did well on the test

exercises.passage: The plants in the garden were wilting. The leaves were turning brown. The soil was dry and cracked.
exercises.question: What can you infer the plants need?
exercises.hint: What does the dry soil suggest?

levels.name: Summarization
levels.instructions: Read the passage and choose the best summary

exercises.passage: The invention of the printing press changed the world. Before it, books were copied by hand and were very expensive. After the printing press, books became cheaper and more people could read. This led to more education and the spread of ideas.
exercises.question: Which is the best summary?
options: The printing press made books cheaper and increased education
exercises.hint: What was the main effect of the printing press?

exercises.passage: Regular exercise has many health benefits. It strengthens the heart, improves muscle tone, and helps maintain a healthy weight. Exercise also releases chemicals that improve mood. People who exercise regularly often feel happier and have more energy.
exercises.question: Which is the best summary?
options: Exercise improves physical and mental health
exercises.hint: What are the different benefits mentioned?

exercises.passage: Bees are essential for agriculture. They pollinate flowers, which allows plants to produce fruits and vegetables. Without bees, many crops would fail. This would affect food supplies around the world. Protecting bee populations is important for food security.
exercises.question: Which is the best summary?
options: Bees are important for food production
exercises.hint: What is the connection between bees and food?

levels.name: Cooperative Activities

exercises.scenario: You're doing paired reading with a peer.
exercises.question: What's an effective approach?
options: One person reads, the other does nothing
Take turns reading and helping each other
exercises.hint: Both should participate and help each other

exercises.scenario: You're working on a group project about reading strategies.
exercises.question: How can you contribute effectively?
options: Let others do all the work
Do your assigned part and help others

exercises.scenario: Your group disagrees on an answer.
exercises.question: What's the best way to resolve it?
options: Argue until one person gives up
Discuss the reasons and find evidence
exercises.hint: Discussion and evidence help resolve disagreements

levels.name: Basic Sight Words
levels.instructions: Practice recognizing common sight words

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: the
exercises.hint: This is one of the most common words

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: and
Type the sight word you see: is
Type the sight word you see: it
Type the sight word you see: in

levels.instructions: Practice recognizing more common sight words

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: said
exercises.hint: This is the past tense of say

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: was
exercises.hint: This is the past tense of is

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: of
exercises.hint: This word shows belonging or connection

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: to
Type the sight word you see: for

levels.name: Advanced Sight Words
levels.instructions: Practice recognizing challenging sight words

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: because
Type the sight word you see: thought
exercises.hint: This is the past tense of think

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: through
exercises.hint: This word means from one side to the other

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: different
exercises.hint: This word means not the same

exercises.instruction: Type the sight word you see: important

auditory-processing.name: Auditory Processing Training
auditory-processing.description: Practice sound discrimination and auditory memory

levels.name: Sound Discrimination
levels.instructions: Practice distinguishing between similar sounds

exercises.question: Which sound is different?
exercises.hint: One is voiced, one is not

exercises.question: Which sound is different?
exercises.hint: One is voiced, one is not

exercises.question: Which sound is different?
exercises.hint: One is made with lips, one with nose

levels.name: Auditory Memory
levels.instructions: Practice remembering sequences of sounds

levels.name: Temporal Processing
levels.instructions: Practice processing sounds in time

exercises.question: Which sounds do you hear in 'ba'?

reading-motivation.name: Reading Motivation and Engagement
reading-motivation.description: Build interest and enjoyment in reading

levels.name: Interest Assessment
levels.instructions: Identify your reading interests

exercises.question: What type of stories do you enjoy most?
What makes you want to keep reading a book?
How do you prefer to discover new books?
exercises.hint: Multiple sources help you find good books

levels.name: Goal Setting for Reading
levels.instructions: Set personal reading goals

exercises.scenario: You want to read more regularly.
exercises.question: Which is a good reading goal?
exercises.hint: Good goals are specific and achievable

exercises.scenario: You want to try new genres.
exercises.question: Which is a good approach?
options: Read one book from a new genre each month
Read only what others tell you

exercises.scenario: You want to finish a long book.
exercises.question: Which strategy would help?
options: Read it all in one day
Set a daily reading goal and track progress
exercises.hint: Breaking it into smaller parts helps

levels.name: Building Reading Habits
levels.instructions: Create sustainable reading habits

exercises.scenario: You want to make reading a daily habit.
exercises.question: What's the best approach?
options: Read at the same time every day
Read only when you have nothing else to do

exercises.scenario: You're having trouble finding time to read.
exercises.question: What could help?
options: Find small pockets of time (10-15 minutes) throughout the day
exercises.hint: Small amounts of time add up

exercises.scenario: You're in the middle of a boring book.
exercises.question: What should you do?
options: It's okay to stop and try a different book
exercises.hint: Life is too short for boring books

exercises.visualHint: Show a figure-eight path

What comes next in the pattern: 123 123 ___?
What comes next in the pattern: A1 B2 C3 ___?

exercises.question: Remember these colors: red, blue, green. Which was first?
Remember these shapes: circle, square, triangle. Which was last?
Remember these letters: A, B, C, D. Which was in the middle?

exercises.visualHint: Show three objects representing the number

exercises.visualHint: Show four objects representing the number

executive-function.name: Executive Function Support
executive-function.description: Practice planning, organization, and task completion

levels.name: Planning Skills
levels.instructions: Practice breaking tasks into steps

exercises.question: What's a good first step for writing an essay?
What's a good first step for studying?
exercises.hint: Start by reviewing what you need to know

exercises.question: What's a good first step?
options: Ask someone else to do it
exercises.hint: Start with the most obvious task

levels.name: Organization Skills
levels.instructions: Practice organizing materials and time

exercises.scenario: You have multiple assignments due.
exercises.question: How should you organize your time?
options: Do them all at the last minute
Prioritize by due date and importance

exercises.scenario: Your desk is messy and you can't find things.
exercises.question: What's a good organizing strategy?

exercises.scenario: You keep forgetting homework.
exercises.question: What organizational tool would help?
options: Use a planner or reminder system

levels.name: Task Initiation
levels.instructions: Practice starting tasks without procrastination

exercises.scenario: You have a big project due in a week.
exercises.question: What's the best approach?
options: Start today and work on it a bit each day
Worry about it but do nothing
exercises.hint: Breaking it into smaller parts helps

exercises.scenario: You're having trouble starting a task.
exercises.question: What strategy could help?
options: Commit to working on it for just 5 minutes
Wait until you feel like it

exercises.scenario: You have several small tasks to do.
exercises.question: What's a good approach?
options: Do the quickest task first to build momentum

levels.name: Articulation Practice
levels.instructions: Practice producing specific sounds correctly

Practice saying words with 's' sound. Type the word: snake
Practice saying words with 'th' sound. Type the word: think
Practice saying words with 'l' sound. Type the word: lion
exercises.hint: Touch tongue to roof of mouth

exercises.instruction: Practice saying words with 'sh' sound. Type the word: shoe

levels.name: Language Exercises
levels.instructions: Practice using language correctly

levels.name: Expressive Language
levels.instructions: Practice expressing ideas clearly

exercises.prompt: Describe your favorite animal in one sentence.
exercises.instruction: Type a complete sentence describing your favorite animal.
exercises.example: My favorite animal is a dog because it is loyal.
exercises.hint: Include what the animal is and why you like it

exercises.prompt: Explain how to make a sandwich in one sentence.
exercises.instruction: Type a complete sentence explaining how to make a sandwich.
exercises.example: To make a sandwich, put ingredients between two slices of bread.

exercises.prompt: Describe what you did yesterday in one sentence.
exercises.instruction: Type a complete sentence about yesterday.
exercises.example: Yesterday, I went to the park and played with my friends.

mindfulness.description: Practice mindfulness techniques to reduce anxiety and improve focus

levels.instructions: Practice mindful breathing

exercises.prompt: Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, breathe out for 4, hold for 4
exercises.visualHint: Show a square path for breathing

exercises.prompt: Breathe in for 4, hold for 7, breathe out for 8
exercises.visualHint: Show numbers counting down

exercises.prompt: Breathe deeply into your belly, not your chest
exercises.visualHint: Show a belly expanding and contracting

exercises.prompt: Breathe in through one nostril, out through the other
exercises.visualHint: Show nostril visualization

exercises.visualHint: Show a body outline with scanning movement

exercises.prompt: Notice tension in your body and consciously release it
exercises.visualHint: Show tension points and relaxation
